image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a metallic green tiger beetle on dry, cracked earth. The beetle has a shiny, iridescent exoskeleton with pale markings on its elytra. Its head is visible with large eyes and mandibles, though partially shadowed. Six legs are present, appearing slender and jointed. Antennae are visible but blend slightly with the background texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head broader than pronotum with large prominent compound eyes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head structure is visible; compound eyes are prominent and bulging, consistent with tiger beetle morphology. Head width appears comparable to or slightly broader than the immediate neck/pronotum connection.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long sickle-shaped mandibles adapted for capturing prey.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Mandibles are visible at the front of the head, appearing elongated and curved (sickle-like), though lighting makes fine detail slightly hard to resolve.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Filiform antennae extending well beyond the midbody.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Antennae are visible but appear short or partially obscured/blended into the background. They do not clearly extend 'well beyond' the midbody in this specific pose/angle; one antenna is curled back, the other is less distinct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated, slender body with distinctly narrow proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is oval-elongated, typical of carabid beetles. Proportions look correct for a tiger beetle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bright metallic coloration in green, bronze, or copper tones.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The beetle exhibits a strong metallic emerald green sheen with iridescence, matching the description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive pale markings on smooth iridescent elytra.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pale, cream-colored irregular markings are clearly visible on the posterior half of the elytra.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Six slender cursorial legs enabling rapid pursuit.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All six legs are visible. They are slender, jointed, and positioned in a running stance (cursorial).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Chitinous exoskeleton with segmented body (head, thorax, abdomen).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The segmentation between head, pronotum (thorax cover), and elytra (abdomen cover) is clear. Texture appears hard and chitinous.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The left antenna seems to lose definition and blend slightly into the soil texture, lacking the sharp edge continuity seen in the legs. This could be depth-of-field blur or slight generation softness.
The very tips of the right hind leg appear to merge indistinctly with the ground cracks, lacking clear tarsal segments. It looks like the leg ends abruptly or melts into the dirt.
